extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, legal counsel, and policy staff
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and implementing the Department of Education's final Title IX grievance procedure requirements (appeals, dismissals, investigations, consolidation, privacy, and supportive measures) for recipients of federal education funding. Focuses on procedural obligations and limits under 34 CFR 106.45/106.46 and related cross-references (e.g., FERPA, §106.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from dismissal required (with conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.45(d)(3) requires a recipient to offer an appeal from a dismissed complaint to parties; respondent appeals are conditioned on whether the respondent has been notified of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.45(d)(3) to cross-reference bases for appeal incorporated at §106.46(i)(1). The availability of respondent appeals from a dismissal is conditioned on whether the respondent has been notified of the allegations; once a dismissal is appealed, the regulations apply equally to both parties under §106.45(d)(3)(ii). The Department declined to require written notice of appeal outcomes but did not prohibit written notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted bases for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of dismissals are permitted on the same bases required under the 2020 amendments (incorporated at §106.46(i)(1)): procedural irregularity; new evidence that was not reasonably available at the time of dismissal; or Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.45(d)(3) cross-references §106.46(i)(1) to incorporate these bases. The Department explains that providing the opportunity to appeal dismissals promotes sound determinations and confidence in grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity related to appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.45(d)(3) requires that recipients notify the complainant that a dismissal may be appealed and, if the dismissal occurs after the respondent has been notified of the allegations, notify the respondent that the dismissal may be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any party appeals the dismissal, a recipient must notify all parties of any appeal, including notice of the allegations consistent with §106.45(c) if notice was not previously provided to the respondent. Paragraph (d)(3)(v) requires providing the parties a reasonable and equal opportunity to make a statement in support of, or challenging, the outcome; paragraph (d)(3)(vi) requires notice of the result of the appeal and the rationale for the result. The Department replaced wording for clarity (e.g., 'of any appeal' and 'the parties').

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality of appeal decisionmaker
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker for an appeal must not have taken part in the investigation of the allegations or the dismissal of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, a Title IX Coordinator is prohibited from deciding the appeal if they took part in the investigation or dismissal. The Department declined to further restrict who may decide an appeal beyond this prohibition, noting protections against bias and conflict of interest under §§106.45(b)(2) and 106.8(d)(2)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal implementation of appeal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a dismissal is appealed, a recipient must implement the same appeal procedures for all parties (i.e., equal, not merely equitable, implementation of the appeal process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department intentionally uses 'equal' and 'equitable' differently: in §106.45(d) 'equal/equally' means identical appeal procedures for all parties once appealed; §106.45(b)(1) separately requires overall equitable treatment recognizing some procedural aspects may require equitable (not equal) treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No categorical requirement for written notice of appeal outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to notify parties in writing of the outcome of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This decision is consistent with stakeholder feedback that requiring written notice often prevents elementary and secondary schools from handling incidents promptly; nothing in the regulations prohibits providing written notice voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective steps after dismissal (supportive measures and prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(d)(4) requires a recipient that dismisses a complaint to, as appropriate, offer supportive measures to the complainant and, as applicable, the respondent, and to take prompt and effective steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient (not necessarily the Title IX Coordinator) has the obligation to ensure compliance and to take other appropriate prompt and effective steps. Examples include convening a floor meeting to discuss allegations while retaining complainant anonymity or encouraging witnesses to come forward. Recipients have discretion to determine appropriate steps consistent with §106.44(f)(1)(vii). The Department clarified delegation is permitted provided the Title IX Coordinator retains ultimate oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures to respondents on equitable basis (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(d)(4)(ii) requires a recipient to provide supportive measures to a respondent on an equitable basis with a complainant except where impracticable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include when the recipient is unable to identify the respondent after reasonable steps, when the respondent is not participating in the recipient's education program or activity and is not employed by the recipient, or when the respondent has not been notified of the allegations. See also discussion of §106.44(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary consolidation of complaints (§106.45(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may consolidate complaints (multiple complainants, multiple respondents, or cross-complaints) at their discretion; the Department declines to categorically require or prohibit consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consider facts and circumstances when deciding whether to consolidate, including toll on parties, fairness, and risk to integrity of investigation. The final regulations provide procedural protections (e.g., equitable treatment, impartial investigators/decisionmakers) to address concerns about consolidation. §106.45(e) should be interpreted consistent with FERPA. Recipients may adopt additional provisions as long as they apply equally to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation must not curtail individual party rights or treat parties as a group
rubrics_metrics.description: When complaints are consolidated, each individual party retains the rights granted under §§106.45 and, if applicable, 106.46; a 'respondent' is defined as a person—not a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient must not curtail a party's rights or weigh the evidence differently due to consolidation. Protections against group-related bias include conflict-of-interest/bias prohibitions (§106.45(b)(2)), required training (§106.8(d)(2)(iii)), and recordkeeping of training (§106.8(f)(1) and (3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and FERPA/privacy constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must interpret §106.45(e) consistently with FERPA; consolidation is optional and may not be exercised where it would cause a FERPA violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may obtain prior written consent from parents or eligible students to disclose education records; may redact information not relevant to the allegations but must still comply with §106.45/106.46; may disclose personally identifiable information to a school official with legitimate educational interest under FERPA (20 U.S.C. 1232g(b)(1)(A); 34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii), 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate, reliable, and impartial investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(f) requires recipients to provide for 'adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of complaints.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision forms the foundation for equitable adjudications. §106.45(b)(1) requires equitable treatment of complainants and respondents and §106.45(b)(2) requires that any person designated as Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker 'not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.' Investigators and decisionmakers must receive training on serving impartially, including avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias (§106.8(d)(2)(iii)). Investigations must assess witness credibility as relevant (§106.45(g)), and recipients remain obligated to comply with procedural requirements across consolidated or separate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative burden remains on the recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden to conduct an investigation and to gather sufficient evidence to determine whether sex discrimination occurred remains on the recipient—not on the parties or the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised concerns about recipients shifting burden to students (e.g., in affirmative consent contexts); the final rules preserve the recipient's investigatory burden. The Department will offer technical assistance and guidance as appropriate to promote compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and recordkeeping requirements for impartiality and bias prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and decisionmakers must receive training on how to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias; recipients must maintain records documenting grievance procedures and training materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department determined §106.8(d) balances required training topics with flexibility for recipients to choose additional content. Recordkeeping requirements are specified at §106.8(f)(1) and (3). The Department expects recipients to document training and maintain materials used to provide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of cross-complaints/counter-complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion to consolidate an initial complaint and subsequent complaints (including cross-complaints and counter-complaints) regardless of filer; parties may file complaints to pursue allegations of sex discrimination, including slander if addressed under conduct codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complainant alleges a subsequent complaint was made in retaliation, the recipient must determine whether it constitutes prohibited retaliation under §106.71. A recipient may dismiss a subsequent complaint under §106.45(d)(1) (e.g., if the conduct would not constitute sex discrimination). Nothing prevents addressing slander or other misconduct outside Title IX under recipient conduct codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction and relevance when sharing evidence in consolidated cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may redact information that is not relevant to the allegations when sharing evidence but must ensure compliance with §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must be mindful of obligations to protect privacy (§106.45(b)(5)) and to prevent/address unauthorized disclosure (§§106.45(f)(4)(iii) and 106.46(e)(6)(iii)). Recipients cannot consolidate when consolidation would give rise to FERPA violations unless proper consent or exceptions apply.
